## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix refresh before merge because adding a file can make verification accept an earlier edit to a tracked file.

## Changes

The pull request adds two helpers for updating the integrity manifest. Refresh fingerprints every supplied file, while registration fingerprints only unlisted files. Tests cover both helpers.

## Critical

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Preserve tracked fingerprints during refresh — When refresh receives a hand-edited `tracked.txt` alongside a new `new.txt`, it replaces the tracked file’s original digest. If the other entries match, `verify` returns `True` against the replacement digest. — Adding a new file can erase the evidence that verification uses to detect an earlier edit. — Fix: Reuse `register_new_files` in refresh and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries`.

## Important

- app/integrity.py:18 — correctness — Write manifest updates atomically — If the filesystem runs out of space while recording `new.txt`, either helper can leave the manifest truncated. Both `write_text` calls truncate the current file before the replacement is fully written. — A failed update can destroy existing fingerprints and cause subsequent verification to fail while parsing the manifest. — Fix: Write the complete replacement to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomically replace the manifest.
- app/integrity.py:25 — correctness — Exclude the manifest from its own entries — If a caller supplies `fingerprints.json` from a scan of the content root, both helpers can record the manifest’s digest and then change its contents by writing that entry. — Verification fails immediately after the update even when every content file matches its recorded fingerprint. — Fix: Skip candidates that resolve to the manifest path in both helpers.
